Rules learned tonight, to add to section 6:

- **`approval policy apply <page> --pr`**, always with the flag, until
  APRV-360 lands. Without it the verb attests and then prints a branch-switch
  runbook. If a ceremony is interrupted after the write, `git checkout --
  APPROVAL.md` restores the attested bytes and the gate answers again; the
  page re-applies later.
- **An edited, unattested `APPROVAL.md` darkens the gate for every session**,
  the orchestrator's Edit and Bash calls included. Plan the ceremony so nothing
  else is needed from an agent between the write and the attestation.
- **The dogfood suite pins the live policy.** A new autonomy on any class the
  pins name fails the amend on the laptop; fix the pin, merge, sync, build,
  then apply. `read.file.out_of_scope` now resolves by rule, autonomy the
  operator's.
- **After a ceremony merges, `approval log sync` refuses** on `APPROVAL.md`
  (equal to main, different from HEAD): `git checkout -- APPROVAL.md &&
  approval log sync`.
- **A probe that dies before it logs is worse than no probe.** Both probes
  tonight (Codex hold verdict, egress proxy reset) reported nothing about the
  thing they existed to observe; each now says so or survives.
- **Duplicate-check upstream before drafting.** The Codex asks had five, two
  and one prior issues respectively; the draft became three comments.
